prompt: How long does the Moon take to spin once on its axis?

options.text: About 27 days, the same as one orbit
It does not spin at all

explanation: The Moon spins once per orbit, about 27 days. That match is what keeps the same face toward Earth.
misconception: Many people think the Moon does not rotate. It does, once per orbit, and that is exactly why the same face stays toward us.

prompt: Is the side of the Moon we never see always dark?

options.text: No, it has day and night like the near side
Yes, because Earth’s shadow covers it

explanation: The "far side" just never faces us. It has day and night like the rest of the Moon; at new Moon it is fully lit.
